target: Учитель сказал, чтобы мы открыли книги.
english: The teacher told us to open the books.
tip: With a different subject, чтобы (chtoby) needs a past-form verb, not an infinitive: сказал, чтобы мы открыли (skazal, chtoby my atkryli = told us to open).

target: По вечерам учитель рисует в студии.
english: In the evenings the teacher paints in the studio.
tip: по (po) plus the dative plural means 'every' or 'on': по вечерам (po vecheram = in the evenings) marks a regular, repeated action.

target: Либо мы идём сейчас, либо не идём вообще.
english: Either we go now or we don't go at all.
tip: либо ... либо (liba ... liba = either ... or) is the paired 'either/or', a touch more formal than или (ili).

english: He who seeks always finds.
tip: тот, кто (tot, kto) means he who: the pointer тот (tot = that one) leads and the relative кто (kto = who) opens the clause.

english: She asked where I live.
tip: In reported questions Russian keeps the original tense: живу (zhivu = live) stays present after спросила (sprasila = asked), where English might shift to lived.

english: I drink tea with milk.
tip: с (s = with) takes the instrumental case, so молоко (malako) becomes молоком (malakom): чай с молоком (chai s malakom = tea with milk).

english: We left before it got dark.
tip: пока не (paka ne = until) marks the point an action lasts up to. The не (ne) here is not a negation: стемнело (stemnela = it got dark) is a real event.

english: We will go if you want.
tip: если (esli = if) here is a real condition. For an unreal one use если бы plus a past verb: если бы ты хотел (esli by ty khatel = if you wanted).

english: Since you are here, help me.
tip: As a conjunction раз (raz) means since or given that, a casual way to give a reason: раз ты здесь (raz ty zdes = since you are here).

english: I used to read the newspaper every day.
tip: The imperfective past читал (chital = used to read) covers repeated action, so with каждый день (kazhdy den = every day) it means read habitually.

english: The dress that she put on is blue.
tip: надела (nadela = put on) comes from надеть (nadet), for putting clothes on yourself. одеть (adet) means to dress someone else. платье (plate = dress) takes надеть.

english: The place we are going to is beautiful.
tip: куда (kuda = to where) marks direction with a motion verb like едем (edem = we go). Use где (gde = where) only for a fixed location.

english: I was told that the store is closed.
tip: сказали (skazali = told) with no subject plus dative мне (mne = to me) is Russian's they-told-me, standing in for the English passive I was told.

english: I will call as soon as I am free.
tip: After как только (kak tolka = as soon as) Russian uses a future verb: освобожусь (asvabazhus = I will be free), where English keeps the present.

target: Он сказал то, чего я боялся.
english: He said what I was afraid of.
tip: The verb бояться (bayatsya = to fear) takes the genitive, so the relative is чего (chevo), not что (chto): то, чего я боялся (to, chevo ya bayalsya = what I feared).

target: Они уехали, так что дом пустой.
english: They left, so the house is empty.
tip: так что (tak chto = so, therefore) marks a result: уехали, так что дом пустой (uekhali, tak chto dom pustoy). For a cause use так как (tak kak) instead.

target: Как дети, так и взрослые любят мороженое.
english: Both children and adults like ice cream.
tip: The frame как ... так и (kak ... tak i) means both...and: как дети, так и взрослые (kak deti, tak i vzroslye = both children and adults).

target: Не только он, но и она придёт.
english: Not only he but also she will come.
tip: Paired не только ... но и (ne tolka ... no i) means not only...but also: не только он, но и она (ne tolka on, no i ana = not only he, but she).

target: Как бы трудно ни было, не сдавайся.
english: No matter how hard it is, don't give up.
tip: как бы ... ни (kak by ... ni) means no matter how: как бы трудно ни было (kak by trudna ni byla = however hard it is). The ни (ni) is not a negation.

target: Отец повторил, чтобы мы были осторожны.
english: Father told us to be careful.
tip: чтобы (chtoby) marks a wish or command and takes a past-tense verb: чтобы мы были (chtoby my byli = that we be). Plain что (chto = that) only reports a fact.

target: Мост, по которому мы идём, старинный.
english: The bridge we are walking on is ancient.
tip: The preposition stays in front of который: по которому (pa katoramu = along which), not left dangling at the end.

english: Without sugar, please.
tip: без (bez = without) takes the genitive case, so сахар (sakhar) shifts to сахара (sakhara) here.

english: In the evening I rest.
tip: For a time of day Russian uses the instrumental with no preposition: вечером (vecheram = in the evening).

english: He works until evening.
tip: до (do = until, up to) takes the genitive, so вечер (vecher) becomes вечера (vechera) here.

english: It snowed all night.
tip: For weather, идти (idti) means 'to fall': шёл снег (shyol sneg = snow was falling), literally 'snow went'.

english: He arrived an hour later.
tip: через (cherez = through) plus a time span means 'after, in': через час (cherez chas = in an hour).

english: He is coming from the store.
tip: из (iz = out of) takes the genitive, so магазин (magazin) becomes магазина (magazina) for 'from where'.

english: We are going to the doctor.
tip: к (k = toward) takes the dative and is the 'to' used for people: к врачу (k vrachu = to the doctor).

english: He came despite the rain.
tip: несмотря на (nesmatrya na = despite) takes the accusative: несмотря на дождь (... na dozhd = despite the rain).

english: During class you cannot talk.
tip: во время (vo vremya = during) takes the genitive, so урок (urok) becomes урока (uroka) here.
